subject: Sizing help: private on-prem GPU cluster for robotics inference
messages:
From: Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@atlas-robotics.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: ava.lin@atlas-robotics.com
Date: 2027-02-11T16:12:00Z
Subject: Help sizing on-prem cluster for lidar/vision inference

Hi Jasmine,

We're working on an on-prem rollout for our perception stack and need a pragmatic sizing recommendation from Redwood for private deployment. High level: we run a 70B quantized model (llama-variant) for sensor fusion and pose estimation. Typical payloads are ~1.2k tokens (after encoding), average sequence ~1,000, but bursts spike to ~2.5k tokens; p99 latency target is 200ms for 1-2 concurrent requests per robot and we expect up to 600 active robots during peak (so ~1200 sustained concurrent inference contexts with rare spikes).

Key asks:
- Rough GPU count (A100-type equivalent) for sustained peak vs. recommended burst headroom
- Network bandwidth estimates per rack (we have 25Gb and 100Gb options)
- Guidance on KV cache sizing, batching strategy, and whether to rely on local cache warmup vs. persistent cache
- Any recommended fallbacks (smaller model variants, routing) to keep p99 SLAs during sustained surges

Attached a short summary of our infra and target SLAs. We're constrained by rack space so we'd like an estimate that balances latency guarantees with hardware count. Can Redwoods provide a sizing sketch and an ask list (logs/traffics/benchmarks) we can send over?

Thanks,
Rajesh
Ops Lead, Atlas Robotics
[Attachment: atlas_infra_summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: rajesh.nair@atlas-robotics.com
Cc: ava.lin@atlas-robotics.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-12T08:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Help sizing on-prem cluster for lidar/vision inference

Rajesh — thanks for the details, this is a great starting point. I'll loop in Aditya (solutions lead) and Dev (infrastructure) to put together a concise sizing sketch and the minimal telemetry we need. Quick clarifying Qs to help us avoid a back-and-forth:

1) When you say "600 active robots during peak" — is that concurrent active endpoints making requests continuously, or an aggregate where individual robots make periodic requests (e.g., bursty telemetry every 30s)?
2) Do you expect many long-running streaming sessions that keep KV caches resident per robot, or are requests largely independent short calls?
3) Are you open to a hybrid fallback (hosted API for overflow) or must everything stay on-prem?

Immediate next steps:
- I'll schedule a 30-min sizing call for next week to walk through the traffic traces.
- Aditya and Dev will draft a 1-page rack-level sizing sketch and a short checklist of traces/logs we need.

Can you share 24–72h of request histograms (timestamps + payload size distribution) and sample serialized prompts (anonymized)? That will let us model batching and cache hit rates.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, rajesh.nair@atlas-robotics.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-13T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Help sizing on-prem cluster for lidar/vision inference — initial sketch

Rajesh / team — jumping in with a pragmatic starting point after a quick run of back-of-envelope math and prior similar engagements. Assumptions (please confirm):
- Model perf: 70B quantized latency ~6.5ms/token on an optimized A100-like runtime with continuous batching; KV cache hit avoids repeated transformer passes for prefix tokens.
- Average effective tokens per inference: 1,000 (we'll model 1k / 1.5k / 2.5k for tail).
- Concurrency target: 1,200 contexts sustained (per your note), with spikes up to 2,500 concurrent contexts for short windows.

Baseline recommendations:
- Sustained cluster: 6 x A100-class GPUs (single rack) configured with aggressive KV cache and batching; this yields estimated sustained throughput ~22k tokens/sec with p50 latency under 120ms for 1k token calls.
- Burst headroom: Add 3 x on-call burst devices (can be on the same rack or adjacent, prefer 100Gb interconnect) to handle 2.0–2.5x sustained load for short windows. That gives total 9 GPUs with burst-capacity strategy.
- Network: Recommend 100Gb uplink per rack if you expect KV replication or remote cache hits. If everything is local and cache warmup is acceptable, 25Gb per node (top-of-rack) with 100Gb spine is viable but increases risk at tail.
- KV cache sizing: allocate for ~1.5x typical prefix memory per active context; for 1,200 active contexts at avg 1k tokens and byte-encoding, plan for ~180–220GB of KV SSD-backed persistent store plus 64–128GB RAM per node for hot set.
- Batching: use short-window adaptive batching (target 6–12ms batch delay) to balance latency vs throughput; enable per-tenant prefix caching to reduce repeated decoding.
- Fallbacks: prepare a lighter 13B quantized variant for emergency routing (p99 degrades gracefully), and a policy to shed non-critical requests during sustained overload.

I've attached a one-page Excel with the math and knobs we used. Action items for Atlas:
- Share 48–72h of request timestamps and payload sizes (CSV preferred)
- Confirm whether streaming sessions hold KV per robot or not
- Confirm rack uplink choices (25Gb vs 100Gb) and whether burst GPUs can live in adjacent racks

We can refine on the call; if you'd like, we can also run a short on-prem micro-benchmark (1–2 racks, 1–2 GPUs) to validate latency assumptions before full commit.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sizing-model-math.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ava Lin <ava.lin@atlas-robotics.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: rajesh.nair@atlas-robotics.com
Date: 2027-02-15T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Help sizing on-prem cluster for lidar/vision inference — initial sketch

Thanks Aditya — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. Quick answers:
- "600 active robots" means roughly 600 robots concurrently sending requests with burstiness (each robot may send 1–3 requests in a short window, not continuous streaming).
- KV: sessions are short-lived today; we do not hold long-lived KV per robot.
- We prefer everything on-prem for now; fallback to hosted overflow would need procurement talks.

We'll upload 72h of anonymized request histograms and sample prompts by EOD tomorrow. Let's take you up on the 30-min sizing call — how's next Wednesday 14:00 PT?

A couple of quick clarifications for the call:
- Please be prepared to show the bandwidth sensitivity — we may have mixed racks with 25Gb nodes and a 100Gb spine.
- If you can sketch a minimal test harness (what containers/bench commands we should run) that'd be great.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

—Ava
Solutions Architect, Atlas Robotics
